long_biography.plain_text:
Financier Mark Garber treated capital preservation as a particular challenge for entrepreneurs experiencing wealth for the first time. He wanted clients to plan succession, spread assets across different risks and retain reserves, while also offering opportunities to invest alongside his firm. Personal relationships and familiarity with both emerging and established markets shaped his approach to arranging transactions.

His collecting followed a more personal rule: he bought pictures he liked. English village auctions supplied works for his collection, which also encompassed contemporary Russian painting. At his office he displayed Scottish colourists, and he kept collecting separate from dealing in art for profit.
